narrative:
The model estimates you have a 10% chance of failing your final year. While this is a low probability, the school policy requires you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The prediction that you might fail is driven primarily by three key aspects of your situation. The most influential factor is that you have had no past class failures. Surprisingly, this actually pushes the model toward predicting failure for you. Among students who passed, zero past failures is the average, but in your specific combination of circumstances the model sees the complete lack of any prior academic struggle as a warning sign rather than a strength.

The second most important element is your strong desire to pursue higher education. This works in your favor and pulls the prediction toward passing. Every student who ultimately passed also wanted to continue studying, so this is a very positive signal.

Third, the amount of time you spend studying each week (2 to 5 hours) also nudges the outcome slightly toward passing, though less strongly than your educational ambitions. Most students who succeeded studied in this same range.

To improve your chances, focus on turning your study time into more consistent, focused work and make sure your ambition for higher education is matched by steady daily effort. Taking the remedial courses now will give you extra support to build better habits before the final exams.
